mainTopic: How many witnesses are needed in a סוטה case, and how contradicting testimony about her defilement is handled
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. It suggests a קל וחומר that one witness should be enough for the first testimony, and then rejects it with a גזירה שוה on the word דבר, so two witnesses are needed. A new משנה then rules on witnesses who contradict each other about whether a סוטה was defiled. The גמרא explains that the word ״בָּהּ״ teaches that קינוי and סתירה need two witnesses, and that the דבר–דבר link teaches the same for plain טומאה with no warning or seclusion. From the משנה it learns that a single witness who is not contradicted is believed, and a ברייתא proves this from the rule that ״עד״ in the Torah means two unless the verse says ״אחד״. Since such a witness counts like two under עולא's rule, the גמרא asks how another single witness can contradict him. עולא and רבי יצחק change the wording to 'she would not drink.' רבי חייא keeps 'she would drink' and splits witnesses who testify together from witnesses who testify one after the other. Finally, the גמרא reads the whole משנה as dealing with people normally not accepted as witnesses, following רבי נחמיה's majority rule, and brings a second version of his view in which, once a valid witness came first, even a hundred women count as one.

steps.title: A logical argument that one witness should be enough for the first testimony
steps.stepSummary: The משנה suggests a קל וחומר. If the final testimony of defilement, which forbids her forever, works with one witness, then the first testimony, which is less severe, should also work with one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The final testimony forbids her permanently, and yet one witness is enough for it. The first testimony does not forbid her permanently. Isn't it logical that one witness should be enough for it too?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a 'maybe we would think' argument: that one witness should be enough to establish the first testimony. It is setting up a claim that the next step will knock down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'final testimony' is that she was actually defiled. Even one witness to this makes her forbidden to her husband forever. The 'first testimony' only leads to the drinking process, not a permanent ban, so by קל וחומר it should be easier to establish.

keyTerms.meaning: The final testimony: that she was actually defiled
The first testimony: the earlier stage that leads to the drinking process
A permanent prohibition (she can never return to her husband)
A single witness
'Is it not logical?', the standard wording that opens a קַל וָחוֹמֶר

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final ruling. It is only a logical argument the משנה raises so that it can reject it in the next step.

phrases.english: The final testimony, which forbids her with a permanent prohibition —
phrases.notes: This is the testimony that she was actually defiled after being secluded.

phrases.english: is established by one witness;

phrases.aramaic: עֵדוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁאֵין אוֹסַרְתָּהּ אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם —
phrases.english: the first testimony, which does not forbid her permanently —
is it not logical that it should be established by one witness?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּים בְּעֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous amud, which is asking how many witnesses the first testimony needs.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that one witness is enough for the first testimony
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the final testimony, which works with one witness even though it is more severe

steps.title: A verse shows that two witnesses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rejects the קל וחומר. It links the word דבר in the סוטה/divorce verse to the word דבר in the verse requiring two witnesses, so here too two witnesses are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'because he found in her an unseemly matter (דבר).' Elsewhere it says 'by the mouth of two witnesses a matter (דבר) shall be established.' Just as there two are needed, here too two are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה knocks down the logical argument from step 1 by bringing a verse. The verse shows that two witnesses are required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse beats a קל וחומר. The same word דבר appears in both verses, so the rule of the second verse (two witnesses) carries over to the first. This is a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches', which brings a verse to overrule a logical argument
An unseemly matter (the wording in the divorce verse)
There / elsewhere (in another passage)
Learning a law from one passage to another through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The first testimony needs two witnesses, even though the final testimony of defilement needs only one. The proof is the shared word דבר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a verse can override what seems like solid logic (a קל וחומר). It also sets the basic witness rules that the next משנה builds on.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Because he found in her an unseemly matter,"
and elsewhere it says:
"By the mouth of two witnesses ... shall a matter be established,"
phrases.notes: דברים 19:15. The dots skip the words 'or by the mouth of three witnesses.'

phrases.english: just as there it is by the mouth of two —
so too here, by the mouth of two.
phrases.notes: The link between the two verses is the word דבר, which appears in both.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 1 with a verse-based גזירה שוה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that one witness is enough for the first testimony
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A logical argument cannot stand against a גזירה שוה from the verse, which requires two witnesses

steps.title: One witness against one witness: she drinks
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If one witness says she was defiled and another says she was not, or one woman says yes and another woman says no, the doubt remains and she drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says 'she was defiled' and another witness says 'she was not defiled,' or one woman says 'she was defiled' and another woman says 'she was not defiled,' she would drink.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on what happens when single witnesses contradict each other about whether she was defiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness cancels out the other, so nothing is established. The case goes back to the normal סוטה process: she drinks the bitter water to settle the doubt. The same rule applies when the contradicting witnesses are women.

keyTerms.meaning: She was defiled (had relations with the man she was secluded with)
She would drink (the bitter water of the סוטה)
A woman (here, giving testimony)

phrases.english: If one witness says, "She was defiled,"
and another witness says, "She was not defiled,"
or a woman says, "She was defiled,"
and another woman says, "She was not defiled" —
she would drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אוֹמֵר נִטְמֵאת וְעֵד אוֹמֵר לֹא נִטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about contradicting witnesses, after the previous משנה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness contradicts another (men or women), the doubt stays and she drinks.

steps.title: Uneven numbers of witnesses: the majority decides
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If one says she was defiled and two say she was not, she drinks. If two say she was defiled and one says she was not, she does not drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says 'she was defiled' and two say 'she was not defiled,' she would drink. If two say 'she was defiled' and one says 'she was not defiled,' she would not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with cases where the two sides have different numbers of witnesses. The side with two witnesses wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses outweigh one. When two deny the defilement, the lone witness is cancelled, the doubt remains, and she drinks. When two confirm the defilement, it is established and she is forbidden, so she does not drink at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (witnesses), a full set of testimony
She would not drink, because her defilement is established and she is forbidden to her husband

steps.whatToRemember: Equal sides, or two saying 'not defiled', mean she drinks. Two saying 'defiled' against one means she does not drink, because the defilement is established.
steps.confusionAlert: 'She would not drink' is not a good outcome for her. It means the defilement is accepted as fact, so there is no reason to test her with the water.

phrases.english: If one says, "She was defiled,"
and two say, "She was not defiled" —
she would drink.
If two say, "She was defiled,"
and one says, "She was not defiled" —
she would not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר נִטְמֵאת וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לֹא נִטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה from equal contradictions to unequal ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses outweigh one. Two denying the defilement means she drinks; two confirming it means she does not drink.

steps.title: Why not use the word ״בָּהּ״ instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier teaching used the ״עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״ verse, when the simpler source is the word ״בָּהּ״, which shows that קינוי and סתירה are not proven by one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why say "the verse states: 'because he found in her an unseemly matter'"? It should have said: "the verse states 'בָּהּ' (about her): about her [defilement], not about the warning; about her, not about the seclusion!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source the earlier teaching gave for needing two witnesses. It suggests a better source, the word ״בָּהּ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה verse says ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״: there is no witness about her. That word ״בָּהּ״ already limits one witness to the טומאה itself, so קינוי and סתירה must need two witnesses. Why reach for a far-off verse about divorce when this closer source exists?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
"The verse teaches"; it introduces a source from the תורה
An unseemly matter; from the divorce verse
"About her" / "in her"; a limiting word in the סוטה verse
"It should have said"; the speaker expected a different source

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This "the verse states" that was used:
"because he found in her an unseemly matter" — why use it?
Instead: "the verse states 'about her'"
phrases.notes: From the סוטה verse ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״, במדבר 5:13.

phrases.english: about her [defilement], and not about the warning,
about her, and not about the seclusion — that is what it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ... מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by questioning the source used in the earlier teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״כִּי מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״ as the source for needing two witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״בָּהּ״ in the סוטה verse is a more direct source showing that קינוי and סתירה are not proven by one witness.

steps.title: Yes, ״בָּהּ״ is the source for קינוי and סתירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the תנא does use ״בָּהּ״ to require two witnesses for קינוי and סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying: the verse states 'בָּהּ': about her, not about the warning; about her, not about the seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא really agrees: ״בָּהּ״ is the source for קינוי and סתירה. This opens the question of what the ״דָּבָר״ verse is needed for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument here. For קינוי and סתירה, ״בָּהּ״ is the source. That means the ״עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״ verse must teach something else, and the next step will show what.

keyTerms.meaning: "That is indeed what he is saying"; the answer agrees with the questioner
The husband's warning to his wife not to be secluded with a certain man
Seclusion; her being alone with that man after the warning

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying:
the verse states "about her" —
about her, and not about the warning,
about her, and not about the seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreement: the suggested source is accepted as the תנא's real source for this case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ״עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״ verse was the only source the תנא had for needing two witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בָּהּ״ is the source for קינוי and סתירה; the ״דָּבָר״ verse is kept for a different case.

steps.title: What about plain טומאה with no warning or seclusion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one witness is not believed about plain טומאה, when there was no קינוי and no סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for plain defilement, without a warning and without seclusion, from where do we know that a single witness is not believed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows why the ״דָּבָר״ verse is still needed. It asks about a case that ״בָּהּ״ does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בָּהּ״ only deals with a real סוטה case, where קינוי and סתירה already happened and one witness about טומאה is believed. If there was no קינוי and no סתירה at all, we still need a source that one witness cannot forbid her to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain defilement: adultery claimed with no earlier warning or seclusion
Believed; trusted as a witness
A single witness
"From where do we know this?"; a request for a source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two cases. After קינוי and סתירה, one witness about טומאה IS believed. Here there was no קינוי or סתירה, so one witness is NOT believed.

phrases.english: And plain defilement,
without a warning and without seclusion,
that a single witness is not believed — from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְאָה בְּעָלְמָא בְּלֹא קִינּוּי וּבְלֹא סְתִירָה, דְּלָא מְהֵימַן עֵד אֶחָד מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6 by pointing to a case that ״בָּהּ״ does not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that one witness is not believed about plain טומאה when there was no קינוי and no סתירה.

steps.title: The דָּבָר–דָּבָר link requires two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the גזרה שוה of ״דָּבָר״ and ״דָּבָר״. Just as the general rule needs two witnesses, so does plain טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Matter" is said here, and "matter" is said there. Just as there it takes two witnesses, so too here it takes two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: plain טומאה is learned from the ״דָּבָר״–״דָּבָר״ link. This explains why the earlier teaching used that verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divorce verse says ״עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״, and the verse about witnesses says ״יָקוּם דָּבָר״ on the word of two witnesses. Linking the two words shows that plain טומאה needs two witnesses. So the earlier teaching's source was correct; it covers a different case from ״בָּהּ״.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is said here... and it is said there"; the opening of a word-link
Learning one law from another through a shared word in two verses
Two witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for two cases: ״בָּהּ״ teaches that קינוי and סתירה need two witnesses. The ״דָּבָר״–״דָּבָר״ link teaches that plain טומאה, with no קינוי or סתירה, also needs two witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both sources are needed and neither is extra, because each covers its own case.

phrases.english: It is stated here: "matter",
and it is stated there: "matter".
phrases.notes: "There" is the witness verse in דברים 19:15.

phrases.english: Just as there it is by two witnesses,
so too here it is by two witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״דָּבָר״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and explains why the earlier teaching used the ״דָּבָר״ verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ״דָּבָר״–״דָּבָר״ word-link teaches that plain טומאה needs two witnesses.

steps.title: Learning from the משנה that an uncontradicted single witness is believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of one witness who says she was defiled. It reasons that she drinks only because a second witness contradicts him. Without that contradiction, one witness would be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one witness says she was defiled, and another says she was not, so she drinks. The reason she drinks is that the second witness contradicts the first. But if nobody contradicts him, one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and reads an extra rule out of it: a single witness who is not contradicted is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says she drinks when the witnesses contradict each other. The גמרא reasons that the contradiction is the only thing that sends her to drink. That means one witness standing alone would be enough to forbid her, and she would not drink.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
Contradicts, denies
One single witness
Is believed, is trusted

steps.confusionAlert: This single witness comes after the husband's warning and the hiding away have already been proven. It does not contradict step 7, which was about plain טומאה with no warning and no hiding away. There, one witness is not believed.

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] A witness says: She was defiled.
The reason [she drinks] is that he contradicts him,
but if he does not contradict him,
one witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּקָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, הָא לָא קָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 3 and draws a new rule out of its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one witness says she was defiled and no one contradicts him, he is believed and she does not drink.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that one witness is believed here.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule it just learned. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the Torah needs two witnesses. So a rule that one witness is believed needs a clear source, and the גמרא asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule drawn out in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a single witness is believed in this case.

steps.title: The verse speaks about two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ is talking about two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: ״And there is no witness against her.″ The verse is speaking about two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It says that the word ״עד״ in the סוטה verse means two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״עד״ here means two, then the verse is saying: there are not two witnesses against her, only one, and the verse still calls her defiled. That is how one witness ends up being believed.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
And there is no witness against her
About two (witnesses)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And there is no witness against her" —
the verse is speaking about two.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ refers to the lack of two witnesses, so a case with only one witness still counts as defiled.

steps.title: Maybe it means even one witness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether ״עד״ might simply mean one witness, since the word is singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means two, but maybe it only means one?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the obvious doubt: ״עד״ sounds like one witness. This sets up its proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״עד״ meant one, the verse would be talking about a case with not even one witness. Then nothing would be learned about a single witness being believed.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a challenge in a ברייתא)
Or perhaps it is only

phrases.english: You say [it refers] to two,
or perhaps it is only about one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁנַיִם, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we should read ״עד״ as two and not as one.

steps.title: Proof from the verse about one witness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings the פסוק ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ״ as its proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: ״One witness shall not rise up against a man...״
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from דברים to show that ״עד״ normally means two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not finished yet. The next step explains what in this פסוק shows that ״עד״ means two.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the proof)
Shall not rise up (shall not be enough to convict)

phrases.english: The verse states:
"One witness shall not rise up against a man, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 12 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That ״עד״ in the Torah means two witnesses.

steps.title: Why does the verse add the word one?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that ״עד״ already sounds like one, so it asks why the verse adds ״אחד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the words ״a witness shall not rise up״, wouldn't I already know it means one? So why does the verse say ״one״?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices an extra word in the פסוק and asks why it is there. This sets up the general rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. If ״עד״ already meant one, the word ״אחד״ would add nothing. So the extra word must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: From the plain meaning
Why does the verse need to say this?

phrases.english: From what is stated, "A witness shall not rise up,"
do I not know that it is one?
Why does the verse say "one"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּשְׁמַע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד״, אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 13 works by pointing to its extra word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word ״אחד״ comes to teach.

steps.title: The general rule: עד means two unless the Torah says one
steps.stepSummary: The extra word ״אחד״ sets up a בנה אב: wherever the Torah says ״עד״, it means two witnesses, unless it says ״אחד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: This set up a general rule: every place the Torah says ״witness״, it means two, until the verse spells out ״one״ for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its answer. ״עד״ in the Torah normally means two, so ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ by סוטה means there are not two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah had to write ״אחד״ to make ״עד״ mean one. That shows that without it, ״עד״ means two. So the סוטה verse is describing a case with one witness, and that single witness is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a general rule that applies elsewhere
Every place
Until it spells out

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's word ״עד״ means two witnesses unless the Torah adds ״אחד״. So ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ means she has no two witnesses, and this is the source that one witness is believed after the warning and the hiding away.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the word עֵד (witness) with the word עַד (until) in the same line. They look the same without vowels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about how to read ״עד״ is used all through the Torah, not only by סוטה.

phrases.english: This established a general rule:
every place where "witness" is stated,
there are two here,
until the verse specifies for you "one."

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה בָּנָה אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and finishes the proof begun in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״עד״ means two unless ״אחד״ is written. So ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ describes a case with no two witnesses, and a single uncontradicted witness is believed.

steps.title: The verse means one witness, and he forbids her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that ״ועד אין בה״ means there are not two witnesses, only one. Even so, ״והיא לא נתפשה״ teaches that she is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah says: There are not two witnesses against her, only one, and 'she was not taken by force.' So she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the rule from step 15 to finish reading the פסוק about a סוטה. Since ״עד״ normally means two, ״ועד אין בה״ means 'there are not two, only one.' Even with that one witness, she is forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 taught that a plain ״עד״ means two witnesses. So the פסוק is describing a case with only one witness. The words ״והיא לא נתפשה״ teach that this single witness's testimony is enough to forbid her.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Two
One
Was taken by force
She is forbidden (to her husband)

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, one witness is believed to say a סוטה was defiled, and she becomes forbidden to her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion sets up the problem in the next step. If one witness is believed by Torah law, how can a second witness contradict him?

phrases.english: And the Merciful One says:
phrases.notes: 'The Merciful One' is a common way of saying 'the Torah.'

phrases.english: there are not two witnesses against her
only one;
"and she was not taken by force":
she is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: תְּרֵי לֵית בַּהּ אֶלָּא חַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 15 back to the פסוק about a סוטה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By Torah law, one witness who says she was defiled makes her forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: How can one witness contradict a witness the Torah believes?
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah believes one witness, he counts like two. So how can another single witness contradict him and let her drink?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since by Torah law one witness is believed, how can the other witness contradict him? But עולא said: Wherever the Torah believed one witness, it is as if two are here, and the words of one do not count against two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's ruling that when one witness says 'defiled' and another says 'not defiled,' she drinks the bitter water. Based on step 16, the first witness should win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that one witness is fully believed by Torah law. עולא's rule says that such a believed witness counts as two. A single witness against 'two' is ignored, so the woman should simply be forbidden and should not drink.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
Is believed
Contradicts
An אמורא who taught the rule about a single believed witness

steps.confusionAlert: עולא does not say there really are two witnesses. He means that when the Torah believes one witness, his testimony has the strength of two.

phrases.english: And since by Torah law
one witness is believed,
how can the other one contradict him?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the second witness, who says she was not defiled.

phrases.english: But didn't עולא say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed one witness,
it is as if two are here,
and the words of one do not count
against two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא עֵד אֶחָד מְהֵימַן, אִידַּךְ הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 16 to challenge the משנה's ruling that she drinks.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that when one witness says 'defiled' and one says 'not defiled,' she drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single believed witness counts as two, so a single contradicting witness should be ignored. She should be forbidden, not sent to drink.

steps.title: עולא changes the wording to 'she would not drink'
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers by reading the משנה as 'she would not drink,' and רבי יצחק says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עולא said: Teach the משנה as 'she would not drink.' And רבי יצחק also said: She would not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by changing the wording of the משנה. In the case of the two opposing witnesses, she does not drink, because the first witness's testimony stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not take back his rule. He fixes the משנה so it fits his rule. Since the believed witness counts as two, the contradiction is ignored, and she is simply forbidden without drinking. רבי יצחק holds this view as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it this way; read the wording like this
Drinks the bitter water
An אמורא who agrees with עולא here

phrases.english: Rather, עולא said: Teach it this way:
phrases.notes: He's changing the wording of the משנה, which said 'she would drink.'

phrases.english: She would not drink.
And so said רבי יצחק:
She would not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר עוּלָּא, תְּנִי: לֹא הָיְתָה שׁוֹתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by changing the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says she drinks even though a single believed witness says she was defiled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading is that she does not drink, because the first witness counts as two.

steps.title: רבי חייא keeps the wording 'she would drink'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא disagrees and keeps the משנה's original wording: she would drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא said: She would drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives the opposite view. He keeps the משנה as it is, so in this case she drinks the bitter water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By keeping the original wording, רבי חייא seems to run into עולא's question from step 17. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks how he handles that question.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage who keeps the original wording of the משנה

phrases.english: And רבי חייא said:
She would drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר: הָיְתָה שׁוֹתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to עולא and רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness says 'defiled' and one says 'not defiled,' she drinks the bitter water.

steps.title: עולא's rule challenges רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי חייא deals with עולא's rule that a believed single witness counts as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי חייא, עולא's rule is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the challenge from step 17 back against רבי חייא. If one believed witness counts as two, how can רבי חייא say she drinks?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא solved the problem by changing the wording. רבי חייא keeps the wording, so the problem returns for him: the second witness should be ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; a challenge

phrases.english: According to רבי חייא, עולא's rule is a difficulty!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא קַשְׁיָא דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge from step 17 against רבי חייא's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling that she drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under עולא's rule, the first witness counts as two, so the second witness's contradiction should not count.

steps.title: Testifying together versus one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that both views fit. If the witnesses testify at the same time, they cancel each other and she drinks. עולא's rule applies when they testify one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the witnesses came at the same time. There, they came one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי חייא by splitting the cases. The משנה is about witnesses who testify together. עולא's rule is about witnesses who testify one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both witnesses speak at the same time, neither was accepted first, so they cancel each other out. Then the doubt remains, and she drinks. When one witness is accepted first, he already counts as two, so a later single witness cannot undo him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
At the same time
One after the other

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי חייא, two opposing single witnesses who testify at the same time cancel each other, and she drinks. If the first witness was already accepted, a later witness cannot contradict him, as עולא taught.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' means the משנה's case, where the witnesses come together. 'There' means עולא's rule, where they come one after the other.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, they came at the same time.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה, where she drinks.

phrases.english: There, they came one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּבַת אַחַת. כָּאן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's rule seems to make the second witness always worthless, which conflicts with רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses who testify at the same time cancel each other, so she drinks. עולא's rule applies only when the first witness was already accepted before the second one testified.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה seems to refute רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when one witness says she was defiled and two say she was not, she drinks. This implies that one against one means she does not drink, against רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if one witness says 'she was defiled' and two say 'she was not defiled,' she would drink. So if it were one against one, she would not drink. This is a refutation of רבי חייא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חייא using an inference from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה needed two witnesses to cancel the one witness who said she was defiled. That suggests a single witness against him would not be enough. So she would not drink, which goes against רבי חייא's reading that she does drink.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
She was defiled (she was with the other man)
But one against one (an inference)
A strong refutation

phrases.english: We learned: one witness says 'She was defiled'
and two say 'She was not defiled'
she would drink.
This implies that with one against one
she would not drink.
This is a refutation of רבי חייא!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: עֵד אוֹמֵר ״נִטְמֵאת״ וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים ״לֹא נִטְמֵאת״ — הָיְתָה שׁוֹתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after Step 21 harmonized the views, the גמרא tests רבי חייא again from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's reading that with one witness against one, she drinks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה specifies two witnesses against one, which implies that one against one would not be enough to make her drink.

steps.title: רבי חייא answers that the second part of the משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא shows that the second part of the משנה (two say defiled, one says not, so she does not drink) implies that one against one means she does drink. So the inferences cancel each other out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא could say to you: by your logic, look at the last part of the משנה: two say 'she was defiled' and one says 'she was not,' so she does not drink. That implies that one against one means she drinks!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא pushes back. He shows that the משנה's last line can be read just as easily in his favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you make inferences from the numbers in the משנה, the first part points one way and the last part points the other way. Since the two inferences contradict each other, neither one can be used to refute רבי חייא. This sets up the need for a new explanation of the whole משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you
And according to your own reasoning
The last part (of the משנה)

phrases.english: רבי חייא could say to you:
And by your own reasoning, read the last part:
two say 'She was defiled'
and one says 'She was not defiled'
she would not drink.
This implies that with one against one
she would drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the proof in Step 22 by showing the משנה's last part implies the opposite.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first part of the משנה against רבי חייא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Inferences from the numbers in the משנה contradict each other, so neither part proves anything about a case of one against one.

steps.title: The whole משנה deals with witnesses who are normally not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the entire משנה is about people who are normally not allowed to testify, and it follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole משנה is about people who are not valid witnesses, and it follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to read the whole משנה, so that its numbers are no longer about regular valid witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since inferences from the numbers lead nowhere, the גמרא says the משנה is not talking about valid witnesses at all. It is talking about people like women, who are normally not accepted as witnesses. In that case, the משנה teaches a new rule about counting such people, following רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new explanation)
All of it (the whole משנה)
People normally not allowed to be witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the משנה is unimportant or is not about real testimony. It means the 'witnesses' in the משנה are people who normally can't testify, and here their testimony counts in a special way.

phrases.english: Rather, the whole משנה is about people who are not valid witnesses,
and it follows רבי נחמיה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כּוּלַּהּ בִּפְסוּלֵי עֵדוּת, וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the inferences in Steps 22 and 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about valid witnesses, so its numbers told us about one against one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about invalid witnesses counted by majority, so it says nothing about one valid witness against one.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: follow the majority when one witness is believed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נחמיה: wherever the Torah believes one witness, follow the majority of opinions, so two women against one man count like two men against one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה says, wherever the Torah believed one witness, go after the majority of opinions. They made two women against one man like two men against one man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי נחמיה's view, which the משנה is said to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In cases where one witness is enough, even people who normally can't testify are counted, and we go by which side has more people. So two women beat one man. This explains the משנה's numbers: they are about majority counting, not about valid witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a ברייתא
The Torah believed a single witness
The majority of opinions (the side with more people)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the key rule for cases where one witness is believed: invalid witnesses are counted by majority.

phrases.english: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed one witness,
go after the majority of opinions,
and they made two women against one man
like two men against one man.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 24 that the משנה follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה can be read as counting invalid witnesses by majority.

steps.title: Another version: after one valid witness, even a hundred women count as one
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי נחמיה's rule is different: if one valid witness came first, even a hundred women who contradict him count only as one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: wherever one valid witness came first, even a hundred women are considered like one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי נחמיה's view, which limits the majority rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the majority rule does not apply when a valid witness testified first. His testimony counts like two, so any number of women against him are treated as only one witness. Their testimony cannot overturn his.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version)
Valid (fit to testify)
From the start, first
They are considered like

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about witnesses who are normally not accepted. By רבי נחמיה, they are counted by majority. In the second version, once a valid witness has testified first, even a hundred women count as only one.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד כָּשֵׁר מֵעִיקָּרָא —
phrases.english: Wherever one valid witness came first,
even a hundred women
are considered like one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד כָּשֵׁר מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רבי נחמיה's rule from Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a valid single witness testifies first, any number of invalid witnesses against him count only as one and do not override him.
